subject: truck2077
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: futuristic militarized truck from 2077.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk, extremely intricate.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a single TypeScript module for a militarized cyberpunk truck, treating it as a static prop built directly in model space rather than a jointed creature, which simplifies the geometry construction.

I'm sketching helper functions for boxes and cylinders, several SVG textures (camo, hazard stripes, decals, HUD screens), and deciding to write my own custom paint functions for countershading and dirt effects rather than relying on external kits, to keep things self-contained. Now I'm laying out the chassis frame with rails and cross members as the base structure.

Working out the wheel placement across three axles, building tires with dark rims, neon glow rings using torus geometry, and lug bolts from small boxes, then adding fenders above the wheel arches and starting the angular cab wedge shape at the front.

Now I'm defining the cab's side profile outline as an extruded shape, plotting the roofline, windshield, and bottom edge points in the z-y plane to give it that angular wedge silhouette.

Now I'm figuring out the windshield as a separate tilted glowing box part, computing its slope angle and normal vector so it sits correctly against the hood's angled surface.

I'm giving it a slightly offset placement and a tinted cyan glass texture with reflection lines, then planning matching side windows for the cab using the same directional approach along the x-axis.

Now I'm working out the side window shapes against the roof slope, using alpha-cut trapezoid textures so the window edges follow the slanted windshield line rather than a plain rectangle. Then I'm moving on to the hood and a heavy front bumper block.

Front bumper design is becoming a wedge plow with angled cone spikes, plus neon red grill slits and glowing cyan headlight boxes positioned at the nose's slanted front edge. I'm also adding armored side skirt panels on the cab and planning a roof-mounted sensor array with a radar dish.

For the rear cargo bed, I'm designing an armored container with a pivoting roof turret featuring twin cannon barrels with muzzle brakes, plus missile pod boxes mounted alongside with warhead texturing.

I'm adding side panel decals like hazard stripe textures, a circular emblem with a chevron skull motif, a "NOVA CORP" neon sign, and a license plate, along with exhaust stacks behind the cab, fuel tanks, cyan/magenta underglow strips, antennas, tail lights, and a bumper to round out the vehicle's details.

For the hull paint, I'm layering a digital camo pattern made from mottled patches in three muted colors, blended with a dirt gradient near the bottom and subtle panel seams along the dominant face.

Adding an accent color and setting up the SDK imports, then defining helper functions for building boxes and cylinders in the truck model...

I'm working out wheel and body dimensions to avoid overlap — rail height, tire radius and placement, then checking cab width against wheel position; since the wheels poke through the cab at ±1.15, I'm narrowing the cab to ±1.05 and moving wheels to x=±1 to clear the fenders.

Now I'm placing the bed container above the rear wheels (bottom at y=1.45 for clearance), checking its height against the cab roof, and planning fender boxes that wrap around each wheel to cover the gap between tire and body at the front axle.

Then I'm positioning the rear tandem axles with proper spacing so the wheels don't overlap and adding fenders for them as well.

The container itself I'm placing between the cab back and rear, sizing it around 2.3 by 1.4 by 3.9 units, giving it the hull paint color, and adding vertical armor ribs plus hazard decal planes on the sides for greebling.

Working out decal orientation on the right-facing side...

Confirming the cross product checks out, so the drawing reads correctly without mirroring on either side, meaning the truck's front stays on the viewer's left regardless of which side you're looking at. Now I'm moving on to planning the hazard stripe and emblem textures.

Still designing more textures: a neon sign reading "NOVA//ARMS 2077" with magenta-cyan glow, a windshield with HUD arcs and reflection, a side window trapezoid, and a license plate reading "N-2077," while deciding to skip extras like a radar screen.

I'm also planning a "UNIT 07" stencil texture for the cab doors and an "ARMED" side marking, then working out the wheel construction with dark tire cylinders and tread detailing -- debating whether to build explicit tread blocks or just rely on cylinder geometry for simplicity.

Still designing wheel details... hubcap, rim, center cap, glowing neon ring accent, and lug bolts, all keyed off which side of the vehicle the wheel sits on.

Now I'm laying out the axles and chassis rails with crossmembers, plus adding under-glow light strips hanging beneath the body between the wheels for that aesthetic touch.

Adding a central coolant pack box with a glowing cyan core between the cargo elements, then working out the cab hull's extrusion geometry, hood scoop and vent placement, and redefining the hood/windshield profile points for the nose shape.

Still computing window geometry...

Now I'm adding door panel seam details, a door handle box, and side mirrors positioned near the front edge of each door, sized as thin rectangular boxes with arms.

For the roof, I'm placing a light bar with alternating glow strips, armor ridge details, a radar mast with an angled dish, tall antenna rods with beacons, and a hemisphere satellite dome, skipping the drone pad.

Now for the front, I'm adding a dark bumper box, then working out a plow shape with a toothed bottom edge extruded across the front for a ram-plate effect.

Finishing the bumper blade outline, then checking z-depth placement so the plough, cab nose, and bumper box don't collide despite overlapping ranges.

Now I'm figuring out the grille's position on the slanted nose face, placing the dark plate and glowing red slits at the right z-depth so they sit flush against the angled front, and positioning the headlight glow wedges symmetrically on either side.

I'm now working out the armored hood plates, calculating the slope angle of the hood line and figuring out the rotation needed around the X-axis so the box aligns with the tilted surface.

Then I'm adding side armor plates on the cab, lower skirting panels, and small details like antennas and rear cab armor before moving to the main container box, which needs a top deck plate added above the existing geometry.

Now I'm placing the turret assembly on top of the container: a ring base, a boxy turret body, and twin barrels extending forward with muzzle brakes at the tips, making sure the barrel height clears the cab roof.

Then I'm adding missile pods on either side of the turret, each housing 2x2 tube arrays with red-tipped warhead cones pointing forward, and a glowing red sensor eye on the turret head, double-checking the pod positions align properly against the container top height.

I'm now working out the rear of the container: double-door lines, vertical glowing taillight strips, a rear bumper box, and a hitch. I'm also verifying the license plate orientation on the bumper using the local axis directions so it faces correctly toward a viewer standing behind the vehicle.

I'm adding finishing details: antenna rods with glowing tips at the rear corners, skipping extra side turrets, considering fold-out armor skirts under the container, and placing thin glowing accent stripes along the container's sides.

Now I'm working out positioning for a magenta/cyan neon trim, a hazard stripe plane sized to match its texture aspect ratio, and an emblem/sign plane on the container's side, calculating their coordinates so they don't overlap.

I'll simplify: skip detailed rib placement and instead add horizontal stiffener ridges top and bottom along the length, positioned to avoid the hazard stripe and neon band. Stacking vertically I'm setting hazard stripe around y 1.6–2.0, neon strip just above around 2.08, and the emblem/sign band around 2.22–2.68, making sure none of these overlap.

Now I'm adding paint seams on the container sides using positional geometry rather than material swaps, setting up antenna rods with simple point-to-point cylinders, and planning draped cable sweeps between the cab and container using a Catmull-Rom curve for a natural hanging look.

I'm sketching a couple of sagging hoses between the cab and container with their own sweep paths, confirming the builder doesn't need bones or joints for this. I'll name the vehicle "Cyber Hauler 2077," keep most paint simple, but use metal finishes selectively on barrels and hubs, while noting glow effects won't work on painted surfaces.

Keeping the palette under 64 colors with roughly 25 defined hex values, I'm setting up the imports from the builder library and its glow and metal kits, then starting to define the camo paint pattern for the hull.

Adjusting the mud threshold so it only applies near the container's lower edge, since the cab and container sit too high for it to show often.

Now I'm sketching the armor plate texture as a darker mottled camo pattern, then moving on to the hazard stripe SVG—a repeating diagonal black-and-yellow polygon pattern across a strip—and an emblem badge with a hexagonal dark background, orange stroke, chevrons, and a "77" label.

For the sign panel, I'm building a dark rounded rect with a magenta stroke and cyan bold monospace text reading "NOVA·ARMS" plus a smaller "2077" line underneath, keeping in mind dark backgrounds stay dark even under the glow filter. For the windshield, I'm layering a gradient panel, a subtle white reflection polygon, and a HUD overlay with green/cyan arcs and lines, dialing the glow strength up slightly to 0.6 for that heads-up display feel before moving on to the side window and door stencil text elements.

Now I'm setting up helper functions for boxes, cylinders, and textured planes to simplify building body parts, then writing the wheel function with tread lugs positioned radially around the rim.

Solving for φ gives rotation angle 90° minus a in degrees, so each lug's box rotates to point radially outward along the cylinder. With 12 positions and 6 parts each, that's 72 total lug pieces to account for in the part count.

Now I'm building the hub assembly: a steel cylinder for the core, a cyan glowing torus around it for the rim accent, six small cylindrical lugs positioned radially using sine and cosine offsets, and an orange cap cylinder extending the hub forward, followed by the cab extrusion using the defined outline and thickness.

I'm figuring out whether bevel settings work with the extrude function and settling on a small bevel for a smoother look, then sketching out under-cab details like steps and a tool box while deciding to keep standard wheels rather than hover-skids for the futuristic touch. I'm also positioning vertical exhaust stack cylinders symmetrically on either side near the cab-container gap, checking that their placement lines up with the container's front edge and length.

Now I'm adding glowing orange tips to the exhaust stacks and a small heat shield plate, plus thinking about a sensor mast grating and armor to hide the cab's back. I'm placing a light bar across the roof with alternating red and cyan glow strips, and working out the position for a radar mast with a dish mounted on the side, angled to point upward and forward.

Next I'm adding a satellite dome as a flattened hemisphere on the roof, plus antenna rods with glowing beacon spheres at the tips, including rear corner antennas on the container with red beacon lights. Then I'm starting the turret, building its wedge-shaped body and gun mount on top.

Still placing missile pods and warhead cones...

Now I'm working on the container's top plate, hatches, vents, and cooling fins, then adding the rear doors with seam lines, handle, and glowing tail lights.

Next I'm placing warning lights and the rear bumper/plate, then figuring out where to tuck fuel tank cylinders between the front and rear axles along the chassis rails, checking they clear the wheels.

Now I'm adding cab side armor and neon front corners, then sketching cable sweeps using catmull curves for hoses running from the cab down to the chassis. I'm also adding roof cage bars and an orange accent stripe trim along the cab sides.

Next I'm positioning a cyan glow strip under the front grille, then working out wheel arch fenders and side skirts, checking that their dimensions properly cover the wheel tops without clashing with the cab geometry.

Dropping unused imports and keeping only what's needed. I'm positioning the windshield and side window planes, computing their centers and normals against the cab outline geometry to make sure they align with the roofline.

Checking whether the window's top-left corner pokes outside the cab's silhouette at that cross-section -- it does, so I need to adjust the corner inward to stay within the body profile.

Checking the window edge point confirms it stays inside the windshield plane, good. I'll add the door stencil plane, mirror arms, then write out the full model, keeping it around 350 lines.
